title: Nurse licensure compact states on Mac: work in several states on one license in 2026
metaTitle: Nurse licensure compact states: one license, many states (Mac guide)
description: Nurse licensure compact states explained: what a multistate license costs, the 60-day move rule, and fixes you can do on your Mac today.
secondaryKeywords: move nursing license to another state
intro: Nurse licensure compact states let you hold one multistate license and practice in other compact states. You still have to move that license when your primary home changes. This page covers how the rules work, what the fees look like, and what you can do on your Mac today without buying any tool. Each state board sets its own details, so check the board you are moving into before you act.
tldr: One multistate license lets you practice in other compact states without a separate license in each one.
After you move, the NLC FAQ gives you 60 days from the move to apply.
Fees vary by board. Nursys verification is $30 per license type per board. Pennsylvania lists $105 to convert and $180 for an initial multistate license.
Do the free work first: a license list, the compact map, and the destination board's own page.

blocks.text: Registered nurses need a license from the state where they work. The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics says registered nurses must hold a license issued by the state where they work. The same agency counts 3,465,400 registered nurse jobs in 2025. It projects 194,700 new jobs from 2025 to 2035, which is 6% growth. Some of those nurses will work near a state line or move during a career. That is where the compact comes in.
Which nurse licensure compact states count for your move

A compact state belongs to the Nurse Licensure Compact, often shortened to NLC. Your home state issues a multistate license. That license lets you practice in other compact states without applying for a separate license in each one. The NLC website says 43 jurisdictions are part of the compact. Implementation status is listed on a separate map, so that map is the source to check before you plan a move.

items: You practice in other compact states on one multistate license.
Your home state is the state where your primary residence is.
You move the multistate license when your primary residence changes.
Each board still sets its own fees, forms, and proof of residence.

blocks.text: The compact simplifies the license part. It does not simplify the admin part. Each board still asks for its own forms, fees, and documents. Before any move, answer two questions. Where will my primary residence be, and which boards hold my licenses today?
Why working across states gets messy

Most problems start on the move date. Three dates can fall on different days. There is your last day in the old state, the day your residence changes, and the day you apply. The NLC FAQ says you have 60 days from the time you move to apply. Some guides count from the day residence is established, so the date that matters depends on the board.

Researchers have tried to measure how the compact affects nurse mobility. Shakya, Ghosh and Norris (2022, Journal of Labor Research) use staggered state adoption. They estimate an 11% increase in mobility for registered nurses in compact states, with a similar increase for LPN and VN workers. An earlier paper by DePasquale and Stange reportedly finds little effect. That paper was not available to read for this page, so the effect is contested, not settled.

NCSBN's 2024 National Nursing Workforce Study adds a wider signal. NCSBN says it was surveying 800,000 nurses for that study. It reports that 40% of nurses indicate an intent to leave the workforce by 2029. The page does not say whether that figure covers RNs only or includes retirement. Treat it as a signal, not a forecast for any one state.
Worked example: how to move a nursing license to another state

Start with the board where you leave. If you leave Florida for another compact state, Florida's board says to apply on the move without delay. It also says you may practice on the former home-state license only until the new multistate license is issued. If you leave Pennsylvania, its board says to apply for a multistate license in the new state within 60 days. It says you may keep practicing on the Pennsylvania multistate license while the new application is processed. Both boards push for speed, but they differ on what you may do while you wait.

Residence proof is the detail that trips people up. Pennsylvania requires you to document Pennsylvania as your primary state of residence for a multistate license. It lists a Pennsylvania driver's license or voter registration as examples. Without that proof, you may receive a single-state license if you hold no multistate license in another compact state. The NLC FAQ says applying before the move can lead to a single-state license or a held application until proof of residency is provided.

When you are unsure which date counts, ask the destination board in writing. Save the reply with your records. Email is a good place for that question, so the answer stays attached to your application.
Fees and Nursys license verification: what the sources show

Fees are set state by state. The NLC FAQ says licensure fees vary and points you to each board's current application. It does not give one multistate fee. Pennsylvania's board lists $105 to convert an existing Pennsylvania license to a multistate license. It lists $180 for an initial multistate license by endorsement. Those are one state's numbers, not a national rate.

blocks.text: Nursys verification is the fee you are most likely to see early. Nursys covers RNs, LPN/VNs and APRNs licensed in participating jurisdictions, including all NLC states. The fee applies for each board where you apply. A nurse who applies to three boards with one license type would pay three $30 fees.

Two other Nursys services are free. e-Notify is provided at no cost to nurses and sends notices about expiration, renewal and discipline. QuickConfirm is a free service that lets employers and recruiters retrieve licensure and discipline documentation in one place.

No verified source on this page measures time lost, grades, errors, or burnout caused by multistate licensing. Some online summaries give a burnout share for the 2024 survey. Those summaries were not confirmed against the original report, so this page leaves them out.
Mistakes that cost nurses time across state lines

items: Waiting until the first shift to start. The 60-day window is an outer limit, and Florida asks you to apply without delay.
Assuming one multistate license covers every state. It covers compact states only, so check the map for each state you plan to work in.
Sending an application before you have proof of residence. The board may hold it or issue a single-state license.
Using an old blog for fees. Board pages change, so use the current application on the board's own site.
Showing license numbers or patient details on a shared screen. Follow your employer's rules first.

blocks.text: A quieter mistake is treating each move as a one-time job. Save every confirmation, board email and receipt in one place. When the next move comes up, you will already have the dates and fees on file.
Setting up your Mac for license paperwork

No native macOS app turned up for Nursys, the NLC site, or state board license lookup. These are browser services, so use Chrome or Safari for them. Third-party Mac apps were not checked for this page. In Chrome, press ⌘L to jump to the address bar and ⌘T to open a new tab. Press ⌘D to bookmark a board page, and keep the bookmarks for each board in one folder.

Keep a tracker in Word or Google Docs. In Word, choose File > New from Template to start from a template, or build a simple table with columns for state, license type, expiration date, fee, and deadline. Share the file only with people your employer allows.

Board emails and confirmations land in Outlook. Search for the board's name in the search field to find them. Press ⌘N to start a new message when you need to ask a board about dates. Keep a copy of every reply so the answer stays with your application. See [Outlook for nurses on Mac](/for/nurses/outlook) for more email tips.
What the sources do not settle yet

Two open items matter most. The first is the count of compact jurisdictions. NCSBN's site says 43 jurisdictions are part of the NLC. The official map that shows implementation status was not available to check for this page, so confirm your state there. The second is the clock start date. The NLC FAQ says 60 days from the time you move. Some guides count from when residence is established.

The mobility research is also mixed. The 11% estimate comes from one study. A second study reportedly finds little effect, and it was not available to read here. Use the estimate as a direction, not a promise for your state or your career.
Where Lazur helps, and where it does not

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about anything on screen, and Lazur answers out loud. Ask where the apply button is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it. Ask how to fill in a section, and Lazur guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click. It does not click for you, and it does not edit your files.

Lazur can also draft text. Hold fn to dictate clean text at your cursor in any app. Research jobs run in Lazur's own Chrome tabs and come back with a summary and a report. Treat that report as a first pass. Check each fee and deadline on the board's own page before you act.

If you work in a regulated job, follow your employer's rules on patient and personal data first. Lazur listens and looks only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer and are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Still, keep patient charts and license numbers off the screen while you ask questions, unless your employer allows it.

faq.question: What is the nurse licensure compact?
faq.answer: The Nurse Licensure Compact (NLC) is an agreement between states. A nurse with a multistate license from a compact home state can practice in other compact states. A single-state license does not carry that privilege.

faq.question: Do I need a multistate license to work in another state?
faq.answer: Only if that state is a compact state and you want to practice there on your home license. For a non-compact state, you need that state's own license. Check the NLC map and the board of each state where you plan to work.

faq.question: How long do I have to apply after I move?
faq.answer: The NLC FAQ says you have 60 days from the time you move. You may apply before or after the move. Applying early can produce a single-state license or a held application until proof of residence is provided. Florida's board asks you to apply without delay.

faq.question: Can I keep working while my new application is processed?
faq.answer: It depends on the board. Florida says you may practice on the former home-state license only until the multistate license issues in the new home state. Pennsylvania says you may keep practicing on its multistate license while the new application is processed. Confirm with both boards and your employer before your next shift.

faq.question: How much does a multistate license cost?
faq.answer: Fees vary by state, so there is no single national number. Pennsylvania lists $105 to convert an existing license and $180 for an initial multistate license by endorsement. Nursys verification costs $30 per license type per board where you apply.

faq.question: Is there a Mac app for Nursys or license lookup?
faq.answer: No native macOS app turned up for Nursys, the NLC site, or state board lookups. Those are browser services. Use Chrome or Safari, and bookmark each board page you rely on.

faq.question: Does Lazur file the application or click for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or operate other apps for you. It can point at a button, explain a form, guide you one click at a time, and draft text for you to send.

costs.title: Application fees differ by board
costs.text: Pennsylvania lists $105 to convert an existing license and $180 for an initial multistate license by endorsement. Other boards charge different amounts. Look up the current fee on the board's application before you budget for it. Do not rely on a number from a forum post.

costs.title: Nursys verification is charged per board
costs.text: Nursys license verification costs $30 per license type, per each board where you apply. A nurse who applies to three boards with one license type pays three $30 fees. Ask each board which verification it accepts before you pay for anything.

costs.title: Practice gaps cost pay and shifts
costs.text: A practice gap costs pay and shifts, and no verified source here puts a number on that cost. The rules still matter. Florida allows the old multistate license only until the new one issues. Pennsylvania allows practice while the new application is processed. Time your start date around the board's rule.

costs.title: Held applications add back and forth
costs.text: An application can be held when proof of residence is missing. The NLC FAQ says applying before the move may lead to a single-state license or a held application until proof of residency is provided. Each correction adds delay, and delay keeps you from working in the new state.

causes.title: Each state board runs its own process
causes.text: Every board sets its own application form, fees, and proof of residence. The compact agrees on the license idea, not on the paperwork. A move that looks simple on paper can need different documents in each state. Many nurses learn a requirement only after they have started the application. Read the destination board's current application before you assume anything.

causes.title: The clock starts on a date that is not always clear
causes.text: The NLC FAQ says you have 60 days from the time you move to apply. Some guides count from the day your residence is established. Your move date and your residence date can be different days. If they differ, you can miss the deadline without noticing. Write down both dates and ask the board which one counts.

causes.title: Residence proof decides which license you get
causes.text: Pennsylvania requires documents that show Pennsylvania as your primary state of residence for a multistate license. It lists a driver's license or voter registration as examples. Without that proof, you may receive a single-state license. The rule means a move can change the type of license you end up with, not only the timing.

causes.title: The list of compact states is still moving
causes.text: NCSBN's site says 43 jurisdictions are part of the NLC. The official map that shows implementation status was not available to check for this page. Some third-party guides give lower counts. Check the map before you accept a job in a new state, and confirm the answer with that state's board.

fixes.title: Build one license inventory this week
fixes.text: Open Word or Google Docs and make a table. List every license you hold, with the state, license type, expiration date, compact status, board, fee, and next deadline. Update the table when a board replies. One current list saves you from digging through old emails.

fixes.title: Check the compact map before you move
fixes.text: Open the Nurse Licensure Compact website in Chrome and find the current map. Confirm your home state and every state you may work in. Save the page with ⌘D. Recheck the map before you apply, because implementation status can change.

fixes.title: Write down the move date and the residence date
fixes.text: Record both dates in your inventory. Then email the destination board and ask which date starts the 60-day clock. Keep the reply with your records. A written answer protects you if a question comes up later.

fixes.title: Gather residence proof before you apply
fixes.text: Collect the documents the board names for residence. Pennsylvania lists a driver's license or voter registration as examples. Store copies in one folder on your Mac. Share that folder only with people your employer allows.

fixes.title: Read the destination board page, not a summary
fixes.text: Board pages are the source for fees, forms, and deadlines. Blogs and forum posts can be out of date. Bookmark the board's application page with ⌘D, and note the date you checked the fee. Re-check the page before you pay.

fixes.title: Set reminders for the 60-day mark
fixes.text: Add a reminder for the 60-day mark from your move date. Add an earlier reminder to check the board's current rules. Apple Reminders on your Mac works for this. A calendar event is another option if your team already uses one.

fixes.title: Ask the board which practice rule applies
fixes.text: Florida and Pennsylvania give different answers about practice during processing. Ask the board you are moving into the same question in writing. Save the answer, and share it with your nurse manager or employer before your first shift.

plan.label: Day 1
plan.title: List every license you hold
plan.text: Open your records and list each license. Note the state, license type, expiration date, and whether the state is a compact state. Put the list in a Word table or a Google Doc so you can update it later.

plan.label: Day 2
plan.title: Check the compact map
plan.text: Open the Nurse Licensure Compact website in Chrome and find the current map. Confirm your home state and the states you may work in. Save the page with ⌘D so you can find it again.

plan.label: Day 3
plan.title: Read the destination board
plan.text: Open the board's page for the state you plan to move into. Find the current application, the fee, and the deadline. Write each one in your list, along with the date you checked it.

plan.label: Day 4
plan.title: Gather residence proof
plan.text: Collect the documents the board names for residence. Pennsylvania lists a driver's license or voter registration as examples. Store copies in one folder, and do not share that folder unless your employer allows it.

plan.label: Day 5
plan.title: Ask one question in writing
plan.text: Email the board to confirm which date starts the 60-day clock and what you may do while the application is processed. Send it from Outlook and keep the reply with your records. Ask Lazur to draft the email if you want a starting point.

plan.label: Day 6
plan.title: Set reminders for the deadline
plan.text: Add a reminder for the 60-day mark and one for the day you plan to apply. Apple Reminders on your Mac works for this. Review the list again whenever a board changes its rules.
